propositions: The query ticket digest is re-sent in the user message on every call of a batch, incurring full token cost despite being identical across all calls.

Moving the shared query digest from the volatile user message into the system prompt positions it for prefix caching, but requires the stable prefix to exceed the model's minimum cacheable threshold (measured at 1024 tokens for claude-sonnet-4-6, not the 4096 documented for Opus).
The hoisted prefix including the query digest reaches ~846 tokens, falling short of the 1024 floor, resulting in zero cache hits and a measured +936 token regression (+5.8% on a 12-call batch).
Ordered-pair judgment semantics must be preserved: the hoisted query digest is named FIRST or SECOND in a reference string substituted into the user message, depending on pair orientation.
Precision equivalence across 12 ordered pairs is confirmed: all relations remain identical and no findings change between inline-digest and hoisted-digest implementations.

The sequential judge loop ensures the first call writes any cacheable prefix while subsequent calls read it; parallelization would require warming the prefix with a completed first call before fan-out to avoid N premium writes.
